Munajat-e-Maqbool

Wednesday

Fifth manzil · supplications 151 to 174

Opening praise

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

We praise You, O best of those in whom hope is placed and most generous of those from whom anything is sought, for teaching us Munajat-e-Maqbool, which brings nearness to Allah, and the supplications of the Messenger. Send perfect blessings upon him for as long as the west and east winds blow, and branches spring from their roots. Then we ask You for what we are about to recite. Ours is to ask, and Yours is to grant acceptance.

How to read

Read this opening invocation before each daily portion. Begin on Saturday, read one portion each day in order, and complete the cycle on Friday.

Swipe right to left to turn the page

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

Supplication151

Chastity and ease

O Allah, guard my chastity and make my affairs easy.

Original commentary 151

This supplication teaches something remarkable: if a person is involved in sexual sin and wishes to escape it, sincerely asking this prayer from the heart will create the strength to stay away from that sin.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 104 · Traceable; rejected report

Ibn al-Jawzi, al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah 554

Excerpt: guarding chastity and easing one's affairs; report adds li before farji. Rejected report; Ibn Hibban criticises its transmitter 'Abbad ibn Suhayb in al-Majruhin 2/154. The cited report contains these limb prayers; it is not an authenticated Prophetic attribution.

The anthology omits li found in the report. The reported attribution is not established as verified Prophetic wording.

Supplication152

Completeness in worship

O Allah, I ask You for completeness in ablution and prayer, the fullness of Your pleasure, and the fullness of Your forgiveness.

Original commentary 152

By asking for completeness in ablution and prayer, and for the fullness of Allah's pleasure and forgiveness, this supplication teaches us to strive to bring our worship to the highest degree of excellence.

Source note for 151–155: the specific ablution attributions are traceable to rejected or very weak reports. Their presence in this collection does not establish them as authenticated Prophetic formulas. See the individual reference entries.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 104 · Traceable; very weak report

Al-Harith, Musnad (Bughyat al-Bahith) 78

Excerpt: all four requests. Very weak according to Ibn Hajar, al-Matalib al-'Aliyah 1/79. The cited source reproduces both the original report and Ibn Hajar's critical assessment.

The wording is traceable, but its chain is very weak.

Exact prayer clause in the rejected ablution report. This does not establish a Prophetic attribution.

The report uses plural taghashshana and jannibna; this edition adapts them to the singular. This does not establish a Prophetic attribution.

Supplication156

Success

O Allah, make us successful.

Original commentary 156

This supplication is even shorter than the preceding one, yet its meaning is immensely broad. It teaches us to ask Allah for deliverance from every small and great hardship of this world and the Hereafter, and for the blessings of both worlds.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 105 · Traceable; transmission with an abandoned narrator

Ibn al-Sunni, 'Amal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah 92

Variant: all; another report reads min al-muflihin. Al-'Ajluni, Kashf al-Khafa' 1/205: contains an abandoned transmitter. The cited adhan-response report has the same request, with a wording variant.

Not an authenticated prescribed response to the adhan.

Supplication157

Opening the heart to remembrance

O Allah, open the locks of our hearts through Your remembrance, complete Your blessing upon us, shower us with Your bounty, and make us among Your righteous servants.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 106 · Traceable variant; weak report

Ibn al-Sunni, 'Amal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah 100

Variant: opening hearts, completing favour, joining righteous servants. Weak according to al-Albani, al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah 2570. The printed text expands the request for bounty; the cited wording varies.

The additional phrasing is not an exact quotation of the cited report.

Supplication158

The best gift given to the righteous

O Allah, grant me the best of what You grant Your righteous servants.

Original commentary 158

This supplication asks Allah for the blessings He grants His righteous servants, with this request: grant me the very best of those blessings. It also teaches us always to aspire to the greatest rewards from Allah, and whenever we ask, to ask with complete conviction.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 106 · Verified report excerpt

Ibn Hibban, Sahih 4640; al-Nasa'i, al-Sunan al-Kubra 9921

Locator: 4640 / 9921 (numbering differs by edition). Excerpt. Hasan according to Ibn Hajar, Nata'ij al-Afkar 1/378; included by Ibn Khuzaymah in his Sahih. A companion said this in prayer; the Prophet responded that its fulfilment meant martyrdom.

This is a companion's request reported with the Prophet's response, rather than necessarily a prayer he habitually recited.

Supplication159

Living and dying as a Muslim

O Allah, let me live as a Muslim and let me die as a Muslim.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 106 · Traceable excerpt; weak chain

Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 7048

Locator: 7/258, 7048. Excerpt. Ibn al-Qattan, al-Wahm wa-l-Iham 3/367: the states of Khubayb ibn Sulayman and his father are unknown. The full opening-prayer report ends with this clause.

The authenticity of the familiar opening words 'distance me from my sins' does not extend to this separate weak chain and its additions.

Supplication160

Protection against hostile unbelief

O Allah, punish the disbelievers, cast fear into their hearts, divide their counsels, and send down Your wrath and punishment upon them. O Allah, punish the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists who reject Your signs, deny Your messengers, turn others away from Your path, transgress Your limits, and call upon another god alongside You. There is no god but You. Blessed are You, and exalted far above what the wrongdoers say.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 107 · Composite from weakly transmitted qunut reports

Al-Bayhaqi, al-Daʿawat al-Kabir 432

Locator: 432; 1/558. Component: Opening through 'Your punishment'; overlapping subsequent qunut wording. Al-Bayhaqi: Aban ibn Abi ʿAyyash is weak; a mursal witness supports the beginning. The report supplies the opening portion; its scope does not extend to the full composite qunut.

Al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 750

Locator: 750; Ibn Hajar, Nataʾij al-Afkar 2/160. Component: From 'punish the unbelievers of the People of the Book and the polytheists' to the end, with reordered clauses. Ibn Hajar: gharib; Ibn Lahiʿah has weak memory and Yahya ibn Yaʿla is weak; basic report has a mursal witness. The historical account does not establish this entire passage as an authenticated Prophetic qunut or as Quranic text.

A compilation of qunut wording with weak transmission; its Prophetic attribution is not established as authentic.

Supplication161

Forgiveness, unity and sincere worship

O Allah, forgive me and all believing men and women, and all Muslim men and women. Set them right, reconcile them with one another, and unite their hearts in love. Place faith and wisdom in their hearts, keep them firm upon the religion of Your Messenger, and inspire them to give thanks for the blessing You have bestowed upon them,

and to fulfil the covenant You have made with them. Grant them victory over Your enemy and theirs. O God of Truth, glory be to You; there is no god besides You. Forgive my sin and set right my deeds. You forgive the sins of whomever You will, and You are the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful. O All-Forgiving, forgive me; O Accepter of Repentance, turn towards me in forgiveness; O Most Compassionate, have mercy on me; O Most Pardoning, pardon me; O Most Kind, show me kindness.

O my Lord, inspire me to give thanks for the blessing You have bestowed upon me, and give me strength to worship You well. O my Lord, I ask You for every good. O my Lord, grant me a good beginning and a good ending, and protect me from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have shown him mercy; and that is the supreme success.

Original commentary 161

This supplication teaches us that, when asking forgiveness for ourselves, we may also ask it for all believing men and women. It also teaches us to ask for reconciliation among Muslims, love between their hearts, and wisdom and faith. A hadith mentions that a person who, morning and evening, asks forgiveness for all Muslims will be forgiven by Allah, and good deeds will be recorded for him equal to the number of those for whom mercy is sought. This prayer also teaches a request that should always remain before us: O Allah, set our deeds right, so that by acting upon this correction we may attain forgiveness and pardon.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 108 · Composite from weak or disconnected reports

Al-Bayhaqi, al-Daʿawat al-Kabir 432

Locator: 432; 1/558. Component: Opening prayer for believers through 'God of Truth'; the compiler adds 'me' at the beginning. Al-Bayhaqi identifies Aban ibn Abi ʿAyyash as weak. Full community section appears in the original qunut report.

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Kabir 9942

Locator: 9942; 10/68. Component: From 'Glory be to You, there is no god besides You' through the final request for protection from evil deeds; some intervening clauses of the report are omitted. Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 2/145: Abu ʿUbaydah did not hear from his father Ibn Masʿud. This disconnected transmission supplies most of the extended supplication.

Al-Tabarani, Musnad al-Shamiyyin 2155

Locator: 2155 (3/234); al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami 6026; al-Haythami, Majma al-Zawaid 10/213. Parallel only: Commentary only: one good deed for each believer for whom forgiveness is sought. Al-Albani: hasan. Al-Haythami calls its chain good. The report does not specify morning or evening, or add the commentary's guarantee that the speaker will be forgiven.

Quran 40:9

Locator: Ghafir 40:9. Variant: Closing request for protection from evil deeds and the concluding statement about mercy and supreme success. Quranic text; hadith grading not applicable. The anthology changes protect them to protect me, then continues with the verse's remaining words.

This joins two separately reported passages. The latter ends with wording adapted from Quran 40:9; the whole entry is not a single verified hadith. The commentary's one-good-deed-per-believer statement has a separately cited report graded hasan by al-Albani. Its added morning/evening timing and personal-forgiveness promise were not established in that report or in the targeted searches.

Supplication162

All praise and every good

O Allah, all praise belongs to You, all thanks belong to You, all sovereignty belongs to You, and all creation belongs to You. In Your hand is all good, and to You all affairs return. I ask You for every good and seek refuge in You from every evil.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 111 · Complete wording traced to a rejected transmission

Al-Daylami via Ibn Hajar, Zahr al-Firdaws 595

Locator: 2/305–306, no.595. Variant: All; the two final petitions appear in reversed order. Ibn Hajar: Khalid is abandoned. Editor Muhammad Murtada Sulayman Yunus and the quoted al-Albani judge the report fabricated. The full text includes both all creation and all good in Your hand. The cited judgment concerns this extended Abu Said transmission; shorter praise formulas have separate assessments.

Kanz al-Ummal 22551, citing Ibn Turkan and al-Daylami

Variant: All, with min before al-khayr in this version. Not independently graded in Kanz; the matching chain is assessed in Zahr al-Firdaws 595. Kanz preserves the complete extended wording and attributes it to Ibn Turkan and al-Daylami.

Ibn Allan, al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyyah 5/15, quoting Ibn Hajar

Component: All praise, thanks and sovereignty; asking every good and refuge from every evil. Ibn Hajar, quoted by Ibn Allan in al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyyah 5/15, identifies Khalid ibn Yazid al-Umari as abandoned. This shorter text does not contain all of the compilation's intermediate clauses.

Al-Bayhaqi, Shuʿab al-Iman 4399

Locator: 4399; 4/97 (Zaghlul edition). Component: All praise belongs to You and all affairs return to You. Ibn Hajar, quoted by Ibn Allan in al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyyah 5/16: weak chain. A parallel appears in Zahr al-Firdaws 594, which records al-Albani's hasan assessment of the shorter text and al-Daraqutni's preference for its Companion attribution. The complete wording is traceable. Its extended Prophetic transmission is rejected by the cited critics; shorter parallel praise formulas have separate assessments.

Supplication163

Relief from distress and confession

In the name of Allah, besides whom there is no god. O Allah, remove distress and sorrow from me. O Allah, I go forth praising You, and I acknowledge my sin.

Original source note 162 · on supplication 163

This supplication appeals to Allah through the declaration of His oneness: O Allah, remove my sorrow, worry and troubles. It also contains this confession: O Allah, I am sinful, yet I go about my life praising You. (O Allah, save me from sins; whoever You have saved from sins has found peace.)

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 111 · Adapted text from unauthenticated post-prayer reports

Al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 658; Abu Nuʿaym, Tarikh Asbahan 2/66

Locator: 658; 2/66. Variant: Opening declaration and relief from worry/sorrow in al-Duʿa; closing praise/ confession in Tarikh Asbahan. Al-Salihi identifies weakness in a related chain through Zayd al-ʿAmmi; the longer chain is not independently authenticated here. The longer report is transmitted through Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar. It reads worry, sorrow and anxiety, whereas the anthology reads harm and sorrow.

Traceable variants, but not verified as a sound complete Prophetic text or as a prescribed post-prayer action.

Supplication164

Mercy, steadfast faith and relief from poverty

O Allah, my God and the God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, and the God of Jibril, Mikail and Israfil, I ask You to answer my prayer, for I am in distress; preserve me in my religion, for I am being tested; reach me with Your mercy, for I am sinful; and drive poverty away from me, for I am needy.

Original source note 163 · on supplication 164

This supplication appeals through the angels brought near to Allah and the prophets (peace be upon them), asking that our prayer be accepted. It pleads our helplessness and need: O Allah, I am in great distress and I am sinful; resolve all my difficulties. It also teaches us to acknowledge: O Allah, I am a great sinner, and I confess my sins.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 112 · Report with a severely criticized transmitter

Ibn al-Sunni, ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah 138

Locator: 138; p.121. Excerpt. Al-Mubarakfuri, Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi 2/60: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman was accused by Ahmad; al-Nasaʾi and others called him untrustworthy. The report contains all four requests; its attached guarantee of acceptance depends on the same criticized transmission.

The source is identifiable, but neither its special promise nor its Prophetic attribution is established as authenticated.

Supplication165

Sharing in righteous supplications

O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, for the one who asks has a right upon You: whenever You have accepted the supplications and answered the prayers of any male or female servant on land or sea, include us in the good for which they call upon You, and include them in the good for which we pray to You; grant us and them well-being; accept from us and from them; and pardon us and them. We have believed in what You have revealed and followed the Messenger, so record us among those who bear witness.

Original commentary 165

This supplication teaches us to pray in a remarkable way, making this special request: O Allah, include us in the prayers of all Your accepted servants whose supplications You answer, and forgive our sins with mercy, well-being and acceptance. Whether Your servants are on land or at sea, wherever Your accepted servants are asking You for blessings, include us in their prayers.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 113 · Very weak hadith report

Al-Shajari, Tartib al-Amali al-Khamisiyyah 1172; Zahr al-Firdaws 537

Locator: 1172 (1/332); 537 (2/189). Variant: all, with small wording variations. Al-Albani, al-Silsilah al-Daʿifah 5986: very weak. The report contains this prayer; its ending incorporates wording from Quran 3:53.

Ibn Majah 778 is a different supplication, despite sharing the opening phrase 'by the right of those who ask'.

Supplication166

The Prophet's rank and intercession

O Allah, grant Muhammad the station of Wasilah. Place love for him among the chosen, his rank among the highest, and his remembrance among those brought near to You.

Original commentary 166

This supplication asks for the station of Wasilah promised to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). It is the exalted rank from which he will be permitted to intercede for his community. How great is Allah's mercy: merely by asking for this, we too are granted the benefit of his intercession, which will be a means of entry into Paradise.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 114 · Variant of a weak hadith report

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Kabir 7926; Ibn al-Sunni 132

Locator: 7926 (8/237); 132. Variant: all, combining variant forms of the three rank clauses. Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 10/115: contains Matrah ibn Yazid, who is weak. Original sources vary between love/company, high ones/worlds, and remembrance/abode.

Sahih Muslim 384

Parallel only: The commentary's general link between requesting al-wasilah and the Prophet's intercession. Sahih Muslim. This supports the general teaching after the adhan, but does not authenticate every added phrase of entry 166.

This expanded formula has a weak report; the sound adhan supplication about al-wasilah does not authenticate its added wording or its specific promise.

O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me and accept my repentance. Truly, You are the Acceptor of repentance, the Most Merciful.

Ahmad, al-Musnad 5354

Locator: 5354; Ahmad Shakir edition 7/190. Excerpt. Ahmad Shakir: chain sahih. Al-Albani identifies Abu Ishaq al-Sabiʿi's tadlis and Zuhayr's hearing after his confusion in this route (al-Silsilah al-Sahihah 2/97). The wording with 'have mercy on me' occurs in this route. Supplication169

The qualities of the righteous

O Allah, I ask You for the enabling grace of the rightly guided, the deeds of those who have certainty, the sincerity of the repentant, the resolve of the patient, the striving of those who fear You, and the seeking of those who long for You, the worship of the scrupulously pious, and the understanding of those with knowledge, until I meet You.

Original commentary 169

This supplication asks for guidance and, in a beautiful way, for steadfastness until death. Its meaning is: O Allah, grant me the enabling grace of the guided, the deeds of those with certainty, the sincerity of the repentant, and the courage of the patient. This supplication will reach its destination and, Allah willing, will not be deprived of acceptance or rejected.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 115 · Variant of a severely weak hadith report

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 2318; Abu Nuʿaym, Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ 1/25

Locator: 2318; 1/25. Variant: Wording of 169 and the beginning of 170 through 'Creator of light'. Ibn Hajar: ʿAbd al-Quddus is severely weak and some imams called him a liar (Amali Salat al-Tasbih 1/48). The anthology has minor variants, including striving in place of earnestness and the final until I meet You.

This is the extended supplication in a severely weak version of the tasbih-prayer report; it is not authenticated by the existence of other reports on that prayer. The original commentary's assurance of acceptance should not be treated as a verified reward attached to this particular formula.

Supplication170

Reverence, sincerity and a prepared death

O Allah, I ask You for a fear that keeps me from disobeying You, so that I may obey You with deeds that merit Your pleasure; turn to You in sincere repentance out of fear of You; devote myself sincerely to You out of shame before You; and place my trust in You in all affairs, and think well of You. Glory be to the Creator of light. O Allah, do not destroy us suddenly, do not seize us unexpectedly, and do not make us heedless of any duty or instruction.

Original commentary 170

This prayer asks Allah, exalted is His glory, for a degree of fear that keeps a person from disobedience and leads him to good deeds. It then pleads: O Allah, do not let me become heedless of any duty or instruction. Do not destroy me suddenly or seize me unexpectedly with an affliction. Grant me a fear that becomes a means of keeping me from sins.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 116 · Composite from severely weak reports

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 2318; Abu Nuʿaym, Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ 1/25

Locator: 2318; 1/25. Variant: Wording of 169 and the beginning of 170 through 'Creator of light'. Ibn Hajar: ʿAbd al-Quddus is severely weak and some imams called him a liar (Amali Salat al-Tasbih 1/48). The anthology has minor variants, including striving in place of earnestness and the final until I meet You.

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 7572

Locator: 7572; 7/306 (numbered 7568 in another edition). Component: Final request against sudden death, being taken unawares, and losing the chance to discharge a right or bequest. Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 2/204: contains Nahshal ibn Saʿid, who is abandoned. Report reads 'do not hasten us away from a right or bequest'; the source compilation has 'do not make us neglect' instead.

Two separate weakly transmitted sources are combined. The anthology's wording is a variant; the final sentence is not part of the first report.

Supplication171

Solace in the grave and mercy through the Quran

O Allah, comfort me in the loneliness of my grave. O Allah, have mercy on me through the mighty Quran, and make it a guide, a light, guidance and mercy for me. O Allah, remind me of what I have forgotten of it, teach me what I do not know of it, and grant me its recitation during the hours of the night and the hours of the day. Make it a proof in my favour, O Lord of all worlds.

Original commentary 171

This supplication asks for comforting companionship in place of the darkness, loneliness and desolation of the grave, and then seeks mercy through the mighty Quran. This same prayer is printed at the end of the Quran for recitation upon completing it. O Allah, protect us all from the punishment of the grave and enable us to recite the Quran morning and evening.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 117 · Composite with seriously weak and disconnected transmissions

Ibn Hajar, Zahr al-Firdaws 284; al-Suyuti, al-Ziyadat 136

Locator: 284 (1/652); 136 (1/124). Component: Opening 'grant me solace in my grave'. Al-Munawi notes an abandoned transmitter and another declared unreliable; al-Suyuti marks it weak in al-Jamiʿ al-Saghir 569. The full chain is reproduced in the cited source. Its criticism concerns this opening report; the attached Quran-completion prayer has a separate transmission.

Ibn al-Jazari, al-Nashr fi al-Qiraʾat al-ʿAshr 2/464

Locator: 2/464; citing al-Arjani's Fadaʾil al-Quran and Ibn al-Dahhak's al-Shamaʾil. Component: From 'have mercy on me through the Quran' to the end, with 'parts of the day' versus 'hours of the day'. Ibn al-Jazari explicitly calls the route muʿdal (disconnected by at least two links). The original author gives both the prayer and the transmission qualification.

The familiar Quran-completion prayer is traceable but is not established here by a connected authentic Prophetic chain. No guaranteed Quran-completion virtue is established by the cited transmission.

Supplication172

Confession and refuge from the Fire

O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant and the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, and I move within Your grasp. I affirm that I will meet You and believe in Your promise. You commanded me, but I disobeyed; You forbade me, but I committed what You forbade. This is the place of one seeking refuge in You from the Fire. There is no god but You. Glory be to You. I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.

Original commentary 172

In this supplication, the servant asks: all my affairs are in Your grasp, and I believe in Your promise. O Allah, I have disobeyed Your command and committed what You forbade me. I acknowledge that I have wronged my own soul. Now there is no one to forgive us except You. By Your mercy, forgive us.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 118 · Variant of a report listed among rejected attributions

Ibn ʿIraq, Tanzih al-Shariʿah 1/307, entry 76

Locator: 1/307, entry 76, quoting a report from Ibn ʿUmar through Nahshal. Variant: all, with omitted intermediate clauses and addition of 'Glory be to You'. Ibn ʿIraq includes it in his criticism of fabricated reports and identifies Nahshal in the chain. The full text is quoted in the primary critical work. This source does not warrant presenting the guarantee of complete forgiveness as authentic.

The familiar grief supplication beginning 'I am Your servant' is not the source of this entire different prayer.

Supplication173

Praise and reliance on Allah

O Allah, all praise belongs to You. To You we bring our complaint; in You we seek deliverance, and You are the One from whom help is sought. There is no power and no strength except through Allah.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 119 · Hadith report with a weak transmitter

Al-Khatib, al-Muttafiq wa-l-Muftariq 857; al-Bayhaqi, al-Daʿawat al-Kabir 1/354

Supplication174

Refuge from anger, error and harm

O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure, and in Your pardon from Your punishment. I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot fully praise You; You are as You have praised Yourself. O Allah, we seek refuge in You from slipping or being made to slip, from going astray or being led astray, from wronging others or being wronged by others; from acting foolishly or being treated foolishly; and from my going astray or being led astray.

I seek refuge in the light of Your noble Face, through which the heavens are illuminated, the darkness is illuminated, and the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, from Your bringing Your anger down upon me or sending Your displeasure upon me. To You I turn for reconciliation until You are pleased. There is no power and no strength except through You. O Allah, grant me protective care like the care given to a small child. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of the two blind forces: the flood and the charging camel.

Original commentary 174

This supplication seeks refuge in Allah's pleasure and pardon. It also asks: O Allah, we seek refuge in You from slipping or being made to slip, from wandering astray, and from wronging anyone or being wronged. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your most noble Being. You alone keep the affairs of this world and the Hereafter in order. In this prayer, the words "like the care given to a small child" convey tenderness and loving care in a remarkable way. Their meaning is: O Allah, a compassionate mother does not let her child cry even for a moment; she constantly watches over and cares for him. In the same way, the servant asks Allah for such protective care. O Allah, You are more merciful than mothers; do not deprive us of Your compassion.

Sources and notesWednesday · Prayer p. 119 · Composite containing authentic and weak components

Sahih Muslim 486

Component: Opening refuge in Allah's pleasure and pardon through 'as You have praised Yourself'. Sahih Muslim. Arabic text matches apart from introductory pronoun.

Sunan Abi Dawud 5094

Component: Refuge from straying, slipping, oppression and ignorance. Al-Albani: sahih. The compilation shifts between plural and singular and repeats part of the straying clause; citation supports the underlying formula, not that exact compiled sequence.

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Kabir 13/73 no.181

Locator: 13/73, 181. Component: Light of the divine countenance, protection from anger, and seeking divine pleasure. Ibn Baz: weak but well known among historians of the Prophetic biography. The anthology adds noble and by which the heavens are illumined to the cited report's wording.

Ahmad, al-Zuhd 50; al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 1446; Abu Yaʿla 5527

Locator: 50; 1446; 5527. Component: Protection like the protection of a newborn. Ibn al-Qaysarani criticizes ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn al-Dahhak in a related route; displayed primary routes contain an unnamed transmitter. The three cited texts preserve the request; their source location does not establish authenticity.

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Kabir 24/344 no.858

Locator: 24/344, 858; Abu Nuʿaym Maʿrifat al-Sahabah 7755. Component: Final refuge from the two blindly destructive things: flood and charging camel. Al-Albani, Daʿif al-Jamiʿ 1200: weak. In the report the explanation comes in a separate question-and-answer; the compiler joins it to the invocation.

Muslim's authenticity does not extend to this whole composite. Its first two underlying formulas are authenticated; later reports have separate qualifications. The original anthology on printed p.100 repeats the singular plea after the plural passage; this wording is retained in the text.

ClosingDurood

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, and grant them peace in abundance.

Note from the Urdu edition

Recite Durood at the beginning and end of every manzil. This is a means for supplications to be accepted. (See page 64 of the original edition.)

Reference review

The source’s instruction is retained above. Praise and blessings before duʿā have support in Abu Dawud 1481; the weekly arrangement is the compiler’s. The specific eighty-year reward quoted with Monday’s Durood has not been established as sound. See general references G1 and G3.

General blessings upon the Prophet are supported by Qur’an 33:56. A general encouragement does not by itself establish a particular count, occasion or reward.
